sections.h2: Where does a Clay County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Sandra Brock, the Clay County Recorder of Deeds, files deeds, deeds of trust, plats, surveys, powers of attorney and tax liens. The office sits in the Clay County Administration building at 1 Courthouse Square in Liberty, and mail goes to PO Box 238, Liberty, MO 64069. Reach the staff at 816-407-3550 or recorder@claycountymo.gov.

The counter is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., yet nothing is recorded and no marriage license issued once 4:00 p.m. passes. A deed signed late in the day should go to the office before that cutoff, so ask the title company how it will be delivered. The county notes that there is no recorder location at the Annex, so go to the courthouse square address.

According to the county recorder page, deciding what needs recording is outside the office's role. Staff check that a document satisfies state requirements and then preserve it permanently as a public record.

sections.h2: What are the Clay County recording charges?
sections.html:
Expect $26.00 on page one of a standard document and $3.00 on every following page. Cash, check and credit card are taken, and the processor adds a fee on cards. A statewide fee change took effect on August 28, 2026 and added a flat $2.00 to recording charges, so older fee sheets you may have saved are out of date.

ItemClay County charge
Standard deed, first page$26.00
Each added page$3.00
Non-standard documentStandard fee plus $25.00
Plat, 24 by 36 inches$71.00
Plat, 18 by 24 inches$46.00
Federal tax lien$9.00
State tax lien$3.00
Copy, first page$2.00
Copy, each added page$1.00
Certification per document$1.00

Source: Clay County fee schedule. Military discharges are recorded at no charge.

The state side of the charge sits in RSMo 59.319, which lists a six dollar user fee collected on every recorded instrument on top of other fees. Three dollars of that user fee stays with the recorder in a fund for record storage and preservation. A long document is priced page by page, so phone the office with the page count first.

sections.h2: Which format rules can cause Clay County to refuse a deed?
sections.html:
RSMo 59.310 lets the recorder refuse a document that misses its format rules, or recorded as a non-standard document for the extra $25.00. The county's document standards page lists the details.

  • Letter size sheets, white or light colored, 20 pound stock, with no watermark or logo and print on a single side.
  • Dark ink throughout, text of at least 8 point, and a typed, stamped or printed name beneath every signature.
  • Three blank inches across the top of page one and three quarters of an inch on the remaining margins.
  • Page one must carry the title, date, every grantor with marital status, every grantee, statutory addresses, the legal description and any book and page reference.

The county asks for the full legal description and says it should not be taken from tax bills. Exempt from the standardization rules are documents signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, papers executed abroad, certified copies and court judgments. The office returns any rejected document with the reason written out.

sections.h2: How do I find or copy a recorded deed in Clay County?
sections.html:
The county's online records live on the iCounty portal at claymo.icounty.com. Register as a user to view images at no charge, while copies must be bought. For subscription questions, call iCounty at (816) 295-1540. The recorder's own line, 816-407-3550, handles everything else.

Records are indexed by name, so a search by street address will not work. The office recommends a property printout from the Clay County Assessor's real estate division, which gives the deed's book and page and speeds up a copy request. The office says its online records run from 1968 to the present. Deeds were hand recorded in books from 1822 until an automated database began in 1986, and imaging of daily records started in August 1999.

Copies run $2.00 for page one and $1.00 for later pages, with certification at $1.00 per document. Orders paid by card can be emailed or mailed to you.

sections.h2: What will the Clay County recorder decline to do?
sections.html:
State statute bars the office from searching for liens or saying whether one exists. Use the public computer at the office or hire a title company to run the search. A recorded deed also stays as it is. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed, prepared and recorded at the going rate.

  • Sale prices: these are not public record here, though the Assessor may give you the area's market value.
  • Building details: the files describe land, so the Assessor is the place to ask when improvements were added.
  • Blank forms: staff cannot draft legal documents, so a quit claim or warranty deed comes from you or an attorney.
  • Foreclosure lists: look for notices in the Kearney Courier or the Excelsior Springs Daily Standard and call the named trustee.

Paying off a mortgage records a release of the deed of trust. The release is not proof of ownership, since the deed from your seller is the document that shows you own the home. The county also runs Deed Watch, a free email alert at deedwatch.com that tells you when a document is recorded under a name you choose.

sections.h2: What should a Clay County seller know about the area?
sections.html:
Henry Clay is the county's namesake, and the county dates from January 2, 1822, with Liberty as its seat. Of its 409 square miles, 397 are land. Its 2020 population of 253,335 ranks fifth in Missouri. Clay County belongs to the Kansas City metro area, with the northern suburbs and part of Kansas City itself inside its lines.

Census figures show 265,032 residents (July 1, 2025 estimate) and 110,443 housing units. Owners occupy 69.5% of homes, the owner-occupied median value over 2020 to 2024 is $275,600 and median household income is $88,468. Renters pay a median $1,243, workers commute 22.8 minutes on average, and 297 building permits were issued in 2025.

Cities and towns include Liberty, Gladstone, Excelsior Springs, Smithville, Kearney, North Kansas City, Pleasant Valley, Claycomo and Missouri City. School districts serving the county are Liberty 53, North Kansas City 74, Kearney R-I, Smithville R-II, Excelsior Springs 40 and the elementary district at Missouri City. Interstates 29, 35 and 435 cross the county, along with US 69, 71 and 169.

Whatever town your house is in, the same Liberty office files the deed. Ask the closing attorney or title company who will deliver it, so it arrives ahead of the 4:00 p.m. cutoff.

faqs.q: What does Clay County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: $26.00 for page one and $3.00 for each added page, with $25.00 more for a non-standard document. These amounts include the flat $2.00 statewide increase effective August 28, 2026. Confirm page counts and card fees at 816-407-3550.

faqs.q: Until what time can a deed be filed in Clay County?
faqs.a: Until 4:00 p.m. on weekdays. The office stays open to 5:00 p.m. but takes no recordings after 4:00. It is at 1 Courthouse Square in Liberty, with a PO Box 238 mailing address.

faqs.q: Is a Clay County deed searchable by street address?
faqs.a: No. Records are indexed by name, not location. Get the book and page from the Clay County Assessor's real estate division, then use the recorder's online search or call the office. Online viewing is free once you register, while copies are paid.

faqs.q: Can the recorder fix a name or legal description on a deed that is already recorded?
faqs.a: No. A recorded document is a permanent record and cannot be edited. To change the title, a new deed or corrective document has to be prepared by you or an attorney and recorded at the current fee.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax line on the Clay County fee schedule?
faqs.a: The schedule lists recording, copy, certification, plat, lien and marriage license charges, and no transfer tax. Ask the Recorder at 816-407-3550 or your title company about any other cost tied to a particular closing.
